video_directives: Give the central $1 character more varied idle motion across scenes — currently the same arm-down pose repeats, relying on background cast for life.
Hold the 'PAID IN FULL' payoff beat slightly longer before the hard cut to 'I'M THE PRICE' so the climax lands.
Ease-in the SOLD tag pops slightly earlier in each crowd beat to sync visual sub-beats with the rhythm instead of trailing it.

top3_directives: Unify the text systems: restyle the '$1' and '$50,000' tags in the same typeface/weight family as the header so they read as one design language instead of three
The header's grey fill over the dark purple sky is slightly muddy at small sizes — brighten it or add a subtle warm rim glow to punch separation
Large empty purple dead zone between the header and the skyline (upper-left third) — extend a building silhouette or the moon glow to close the gap
Fix the collision: the '$9,000,000' tag overlaps/clips into the '$1' sign — reposition or animate them apart
Separate the '$4,000' and '$12,000' labels — they nearly stack on the same characters' heads creating a double-tag cluster
Move the '$1' badge off the character's face-to-ceiling seam and give it a stronger outline/glow so the key figure reads instantly at 6 inches
Move the title banner fully on-canvas or crop it deliberately at the frame edge — the tilted plate clipping top-right reads as an accident
Kill the half-visible second arm behind the coffin lid; it creates an asymmetric limb silhouette that looks like a rigging error
Add subtle rim-light or brighter edge on the dark coffin shape — it merges with the dark navy buildings on the left side of the body
The right-edge '$1' tag is clipped by the frame edge and half-occluded by the door — nudge it fully into frame or remove it
Slightly boost the header pill's drop shadow so it separates from the hazy sky/moon behind it at small screen sizes
The bottom third is a large empty dead zone — add subtle street texture, reflections, or foreground rain streaks to anchor the lower composition
Fill the dead top 30% of the frame (empty sky above the moon/price tag) — either push the character+sign composition upward or add atmospheric depth like faint clouds/rain streaks

Increase separation on the background $1 signs and sad figures — their lower contrast is good for depth but right now they read as mushy smudges; lift their sign luminosity slightly so the visual gag lands on a phone
Anchor the character with a slightly stronger ground shadow/contact glow so the focal figure doesn't feel pasted onto the pavement
Fix the cropped side characters bleeding off both edges — their cut-off heads and arms read as layout accidents, not intentional framing
Align the $2,000 and $50,000 tags to a consistent height and left/right margin so the price comparison reads as a deliberate system
Add a subtle vignette or dim the buildings behind the $50,000 tag — the dark-on-dark tag-to-building edge mushes on small screens
Fix clipped labels: '$2,000' and '$12,000' tags run off the left/right frame edges — reposition tags fully inside safe margins
Tighten character edges: the '$1' figure's robe has a stray yellow seam outline and rough rim glow inconsistent with the clean left pair
Fill the top third: large empty sky above the scene reads as a dead zone — raise subject scale or add subtle skyline/moon depth layer
Enlarge the '$1,000' tag — it is half the size of the '$1' tag yet carries the payoff; equalize visual weight or move it nearer the focal group
Fill the large empty sky zone (top 30% of frame) — moon is tiny and isolated; add skyline glow or framing element to reduce the dead zone
Strengthen focal separation on the central $1 character — background characters overlap its glow outline; add rim light or darken the flanking SOLD pair
The $1 sign floats ambiguously above the left character — anchor it visually to a character or action so its meaning reads instantly
Dark buildings against dark night sky create mushy background separation — lift midground building values or add rim light to carve silhouettes for daylight phone viewing
Two equally weighted characters split the focal point — push one slightly forward/larger or brighten its glow to establish a single primary subject
Fill or compress the upper ~35% dead zone (sky/moon) — either crop the frame lower, raise the skyline, or place a title/loop element up top so the vertical canvas isn't 1/3 empty

Boost overall scene exposure or add a subtle background gradient/vignette behind the crowd — as-is, the dark-on-dark buildings risk muddying on a 6-inch screen in daylight; keep the glow rims but lift midtones

Consolidate the repeated SOLD tags: keep at most two fully legible (one on the focal $1 character, one midground) and fade/blur the clipped edge ones ("LD", "OLD") which currently read as accidental artifacts at the right frame edge
Top ~40% of frame is near-empty gradient sky — raise characters or add moon/glow interest to kill the dead zone
Two equal-weight characters compete for focal attention — push one forward with scale, lighting, or motion so the eye has a starting point
$1 sign above the left character floats ambiguously — anchor it with a connector or place it directly over the head for cleaner read
Move focal bill slightly upward/closer to the vertical center-third so it doesn't straddle the middle dead band
Add subtle drop shadow or rim light under the bill to separate it from the same-value dark building shapes
Fill the large empty sky zone (top ~35%) with atmospheric detail (stars, gradient texture, or subtle cloud) to reduce dead space
Fill the large empty sky band between the header and the $1/character zone — a subtle skyline glow, rain streaks, or a light beam would remove the dead zone
Raise the header banner's palette tie-in: the generic dark pill reads as a template — echo the scene's orange rim-light as a border or accent to unify text with the art
Strengthen focal clarity: the $1 tag and the hat character compete — enlarge the $1 tag slightly and angle it toward the hooded figure to force the eye path tag → face → buyer
Fill or compress the top ~40% empty gradient sky — add subtle atmosphere (moon glow emphasis, skyline extension, or floating UI motif) to eliminate the large dead zone above the city.
The small '$1' tag on the left character reads as noise and competes with the central '$1' sign — remove it or visually mute it so the focal character owns the number.
Ground the foreground cast with stronger contact shadows/depth separation from background buildings; right-edge character is cropped awkwardly — either fully frame or push it further back.
